questions.question: An umbrella is marked for Rs. 150 and sold for Rs. 138. The rate of discount is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Discount amount = Marked Price − Selling Price = 150 − 138 = 12

Discount % = (Discount ÷ Marked Price) × 100

Discount % = (12 ÷ 150) × 100 = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Marked Price (MP) = ₹150

Selling Price (SP) = ₹138

**Formula Used:**

Discount Percentage = [(Marked Price − Selling Price) ÷ Marked Price] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f06a8b2f4052ca5ddfa1abd4ce49f9fdf81a34f2db184c663b842790acaab2e6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Discount = 150 − 138

⇒ Discount = ₹12

⇒ Discount % = (12 ÷ 150) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (4 ÷ 50) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 4 × 2

⇒ Discount % = 8%

**∴ The correct answer is 8%.**

**__Additional Information__**

Marked Price (MP)

The price printed on the label of an article is known as the Marked Price or List Price. Discount is always calculated on this price.

Selling Price (SP) formula

SP = MP − Discount. If a discount % is given, then SP = MP × (100 − Discount %) ÷ 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − d₁d₂/100)%.

questions.question: When an article is sold for Rs. 355, there is a loss of 29%. To gain 21% it should be sold for Rs.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Loss of 29% means SP₁ is 71% of CP.

Desired Gain of 21% means SP₂ must be 121% of CP.

71% → ₹355

1% → 355 ÷ 71 = 5

121% → 5 × 121 = 605

**∴ The correct answer is ₹605.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price (SP₁) = ₹355

Loss% = 29%

Desired Gain% = 21%

**Formula Used:**

CP = [SP × 100] ÷ [100 − Loss%]

New SP = [CP × (100 + Gain%)] ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/6882047853d8a41db2f942e7789fc6e09c8f7a37abe9e6d937b2651a8d3f27ec.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ First, calculate Cost Price (CP):

⇒ CP = [355 × 100] ÷ [100 − 29]

⇒ CP = [355 × 100] ÷ 71

⇒ CP = 5 × 100 = ₹500

⇒ Now, calculate required Selling Price (SP₂) for 21% gain:

⇒ SP₂ = [500 × (100 + 21)] ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = [500 × 121] ÷ 100

⇒ SP₂ = 5 × 121 = ₹605

**∴ The correct answer is ₹605.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Direct SP Ratio Relation

When CP is constant, SP₁ ÷ (100 ± P/L₁%) = SP₂ ÷ (100 ± P/L₂%). This allows solving without calculating CP.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit% = (SP − CP) ÷ CP × 100 and Loss% = (CP − SP) ÷ CP × 100. Both are always calculated on CP unless stated otherwise.

Marked Price and Discount

SP = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100. Discounts are always calculated on the Marked Price (MP).

questions.question: What price should Neeraj mark on a shirt that costs Rs. 840, so as to earn a profit of 18% after allowing a discount of 16% on the marked price?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP to MP is given by: CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 16) : (100 + 18) = 84 : 118

Given CP = 84 units = Rs. 840 → 1 unit = Rs. 10

Marked Price (MP) = 118 units = 118 × 10 = Rs. 1,180

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 840

Profit% = 18%

Discount% = 16%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%) ÷ 100

Marked Price (MP) = SP × 100 ÷ (100 − Discount%)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/24a2bee35a0720df6df37ba9862ddb4f745bf8cff157470806ba70e8135781b8.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ SP = 840 × (118 ÷ 100)

⇒ SP = 840 × 1.18 = Rs. 991.20

⇒ MP = 991.20 × 100 ÷ (100 − 16)

⇒ MP = 991.20 × 100 ÷ 84

⇒ MP = 99120 ÷ 84

⇒ MP = Rs. 1,180

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 1,180.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Mark-up Percentage

It is the percentage by which the cost price is increased to reach the marked price: Mark-up% = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the effective discount is: d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Net Profit with Markup and Discount

If an item is marked up by M% and then a discount of D% is offered, the Net Profit% = M − D − (M × D) ÷ 100.</p

questions.question: Anu sold an article for Rs. 480 at some profit. Had she sold it for Rs. 400, then there would have been a loss equal to one-third of the initial profit. What was the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Rs. 420**__
**__Key Points__**
__

• Let the **Cost Price (CP)** of the article be **x**.

• In the first scenario, the **Selling Price (SP₁)** is **Rs. 480** and there is a **Profit**.

**Profit = SP₁ − CP = 480 − x**

• In the second scenario, the **Selling Price (SP₂)** is **Rs. 400** and there is a **Loss**.

**Loss = CP − SP₂ = x − 400**

• According to the question, the **Loss** is equal to **one-third** of the initial **Profit**.

Equation: **Loss = (1/3) ∗ Profit**

x − 400 = (1/3) ∗ (480 − x)

• To solve for **x**, multiply both sides by 3:

3 ∗ (x − 400) = 480 − x

3x − 1200 = 480 − x

• Rearrange the terms to isolate **x**:

3x + x = 480 + 1200

4x = 1680

• Divide by 4:

**x = 1680 ÷ 4 = 420**

• Therefore, the **Cost Price** of the article is **Rs. 420**.

**Additional Information__**

• **Profit** occurs when the **Selling Price** is greater than the **Cost Price**.

• **Loss** occurs when the **Cost Price** is greater than the **Selling Price**.

• **Profit Percentage** = (Profit ÷ Cost Price) ∗ 100.

• **Loss Percentage** = (Loss ÷ Cost Price) ∗ 100.

• In this specific problem, if the cost price is **Rs. 420**, the profit at **Rs. 480** is **Rs. 60**, and the loss at **Rs. 400** is **Rs. 20**. Indeed, 20 is **one-third** of 60.

questions.question: An article is marked 35% above its cost. If a profit of 20% is earned by selling the article, then the discount per cent offered on the marked price of the article is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100.

Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35 = 135.

Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 20 = 120 (since Profit = 20%).

Discount = MP − SP = 135 − 120 = 15.

Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100 = (15 ÷ 135) × 100 = 100/9 % = 11 1/9 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup Percentage = 35%

Profit Percentage = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = CP × (1 + Profit/100)

Marked Price (MP) = CP × (1 + Markup/100)

Discount % = [(MP − SP) ÷ MP] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4ef83d04b8219bee78f99fa112f8ee9d1c21c998f3acda7097c75591636bffa6.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be ₹100.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 35% of 100 = 100 + 35 = ₹135.

⇒ Profit = 20% on Cost Price.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = 100 + 20% of 100 = 100 + 20 = ₹120.

⇒ Discount offered on Marked Price = MP − SP

⇒ Discount = 135 − 120 = ₹15.

⇒ Discount % = (Discount ÷ MP) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (15 ÷ 135) × 100

⇒ Discount % = (1 ÷ 9) × 100

⇒ Discount % = 100/9 % = 11 1/9 %.

**∴ The correct answer is 11 1/9 %.**

**__Additional Information__**

The CP-MP Relationship

The ratio of Marked Price to Cost Price can be expressed as: MP ÷ CP = (100 + Profit %) ÷ (100 − Discount %).

Effective Profit Formula

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − [(Markup % × Discount %) ÷ 100]. This is derived from the successive percentage change formula.

Discount Calculation

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP), whereas Profit or Loss is generally calculated on the Cost Price (CP).

questions.question: A shopkeeper marks an article at such a price that after giving a discount of 12(1)/(2)% on the marked price, he still earns a profit of 15%. If the cost price of the article is Rs. 385, then the sum of the marked price and the selling price (in Rs.) of the article is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of CP : MP = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%)

CP : MP = (100 − 12.5) : (100 + 15) = 87.5 : 115 = 7 : 9.2 = 35 : 46

Given 35 units = ₹385 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹11

MP = 46 × 11 = ₹506 | SP = 385 × 1.15 = ₹442.75

Sum = MP + SP = 506 + 442.75 = ₹948.75

**∴ The correct answer is ₹948.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = ₹385

Profit% = 15%

Discount% = 12.5% = 1/8

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cd9efb22ca88d27a83da3f89e8c1056c51f022dac4b7ab7de3335dfa8d3cd996.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = CP × (100 + Profit%)/100

⇒ SP = 385 × (115/100) = 385 × 1.15

⇒ SP = ₹442.75

⇒ Marked Price (MP) × (100 − Discount%)/100 = SP

⇒ MP × (87.5/100) = 442.75

⇒ MP = (442.75 × 100) ÷ 87.5

⇒ MP = 44275 ÷ 87.5 = ₹506

⇒ Sum = MP + SP

⇒ Sum = 506 + 442.75 = ₹948.75

**∴ The correct answer is ₹948.75.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The direct ratio between Cost Price and Marked Price is given by CP/MP = (100 − Discount%) / (100 + Profit%).

Marked Price (MP)

It is the price displayed on the label. MP = SP + Discount = CP + Markup.

Effective Discount

Successive discounts of a% and b% result in a single discount of [a + b − (a×b)/100]%.

questions.question: A shopkeeper bought 120 quintals of wheat. 20% of it was sold at 25% loss. At what percent gain should he sell the rest to gain 25% on the whole transaction?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of quantities = 20% : 80% = 1 : 4 (Total = 5 parts)

Net gain required on 5 parts = 5 × 25% = 125%

Actual gain/loss on 1 part = 1 × (−25%) = −25%

Balance gain required on 4 parts = 125% − (−25%) = 150%

Required gain % on rest = 150% ÷ 4 = 37.5% = 37½%

**∴ The correct answer is 37½%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Total wheat = 120 quintals | Part 1 = 20% at 25% loss | Target overall gain = 25%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/12db7f4fa82df203140b90a10bebca998db6b7a47a6229b2e55f57105022647a.png] 

Assume CP of 120 quintals = ₹12000 (at ₹100/quintal)

⇒ Total Target SP = 12000 × (125/100) = ₹15000

⇒ CP of 20% wheat (24 quintals) = ₹2400

⇒ SP of 20% wheat = 2400 × (75/100) = ₹1800

⇒ Remaining SP required = 15000 − 1800 = ₹13200

⇒ CP of remaining wheat (96 quintals) = ₹9600

⇒ Gain required on rest = 13200 − 9600 = ₹3600

⇒ Required Gain % = (3600 ÷ 9600) × 100

⇒ Required Gain % = 37.5% = 37½%

**∴ The correct answer is 37½%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Weighted Average Profit/Loss Formula

Overall Gain/Loss % = (n₁p₁ + n₂p₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂), where n is quantity and p is profit/loss percentage (take loss as negative).

Successive Profit/Loss

When there are successive changes of a% and b%, the net change is [a + b + (a×b)/100] %.

Markup and Discount Relation

Profit % = Markup % − Discount % − (Markup × Discount) ÷ 100.

questions.question: A shopkeeper allows 28% discount on the marked price of an article and still makes a profit of 20% If he gains Rs. 30.80 on the sale of one article, then what will be the cost price of the article?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Profit % = 20%

Actual Profit = ₹30.80

20% of CP = 30.80

Cost Price (100% of CP) = 30.80 × 5 = ₹154

**∴ The correct answer is ₹154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Discount = 28% of Marked Price

Profit % = 20%

Profit Amount = ₹30.80

**Formula:**

Profit = Profit % × Cost Price (CP)

Cost Price (CP) = (Profit ÷ Profit %) × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1afb9d09d89f7d8115264b191397f3a8041aa43d6a1ae92e24ebb5d368cd894f.png] 

Calculation:

⇒ Profit = 20% of Cost Price

⇒ ₹30.80 = (20 ÷ 100) × CP

⇒ ₹30.80 = (1 ÷ 5) × CP

⇒ CP = 30.80 × 5

⇒ CP = ₹154.00

**∴ The correct answer is ₹154.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price and Marked Price Relationship

CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount %) ÷ (100 + Profit %). This ratio is extremely useful when both discount and profit percentages are provided to find the CP or MP directly.

Mark-up Percentage

Mark-up % = [(MP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100. It represents how much higher the marked price is set above the cost price.

Discount Amount

Discount = Marked Price − Selling Price. Note that profit and loss are always calculated on CP (unless specified otherwise), while discount is always calculated on MP.

questions.question: A person sells an article at 16% below its cost price. Had he sold it for Rs. 33 more, he would have gained 14%. To gain 25%, he should sell the article for∶
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Net difference in percentage = Gain % − Loss % = 14% − (−16%) = 30%.

Given that 30% of CP = Rs. 33.

Target SP to gain 25% = 125% of CP.

Value of 125% = (33 ÷ 30) × 125 = 1.1 × 125 = 137.5.

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 137.5.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Initial Loss = 16%

Potential Gain = 14%

Difference in Selling Price = Rs. 33

Target Gain = 25%

**Formula Used:**

SP = CP × (100 ± Profit/Loss %)/100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0eb95bda70bc8f7a51e43d5c1e20d07ad0cdcba36edbc0145c6e007fb45947d4.png] 

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) be 100 units.

⇒ Initial Selling Price (SP₁) = 100 − 16 = 84 units

⇒ Second Selling Price (SP₂) = 100 + 14 = 114 units

⇒ Difference in SP = 114 − 84 = 30 units

⇒ According to question, 30 units = Rs. 33

⇒ 1 unit = 33 ÷ 30 = Rs. 1.1

⇒ Required Selling Price (to gain 25%) = 100 + 25 = 125 units

⇒ New Selling Price = 125 × 1.1 = Rs. 137.5

**∴ The correct answer is Rs. 137.5.**

**__Additional Information__**

Profit and Loss Percentage

Profit or Loss is always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit/CP) × 100.

Marked Price and Discount

Discount is always allowed on the Marked Price (MP). SP = MP − Discount.

Relation between CP and MP

CP/MP = (100 − Discount%)/(100 + Profit%). This ratio is useful for solving complex markup and discount problems directly.</p

questions.question: A dealer gains 20% by selling an article at 25% discount on its marked price. If the cost price of the article is decreased by 15%, how much discount percentage should he now give on the same marked price so as to earn the same percentage of profit as before?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP : MP ratio = (100 − Discount%) : (100 + Profit%) = 75 : 120 = 5 : 8.

Let initial CP = 500 and MP = 800.

New CP = 500 − 15% of 500 = 425.

New SP (to keep 20% profit) = 425 × 1.2 = 510.

New Discount = 800 − 510 = 290.

New Discount % = (290 ÷ 800) × 100 = 36.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Initial Profit = 20%, Initial Discount = 25%, CP decrease = 15%.

**Formula Used:** CP = MP × (100 − D%) ÷ (100 + P%) | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/68e0c60658bebd942ded8b942a57fb8d7e308dc777d03b991faebecfab24ce14.png] 

⇒ Let the initial cost price (CP₁) be ₹100.

⇒ Initial selling price (SP₁) = 100 + 20% of 100 = ₹120.

⇒ Initial marked price (MP) = (SP₁ × 100) ÷ (100 − 25) = (120 × 100) ÷ 75 = ₹160.

⇒ New cost price (CP₂) = 100 − 15% of 100 = ₹85.

⇒ Required new profit percentage = 20%.

⇒ New required selling price (SP₂) = 85 + 20% of 85 = 85 + 17 = ₹102.

⇒ New discount amount = MP − SP₂ = 160 − 102 = ₹58.

⇒ New discount percentage = (58 ÷ 160) × 100 = 36.25%.

**∴ The correct answer is 36.25%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

CP and MP Relationship

The ratio of Cost Price to Marked Price is always CP/MP = (100 − D%) / (100 + P%), where D is discount and P is profit.

Successive Discounts

If two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given, the single equivalent discount is (d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂)/100)%.

Markup Percentage

Markup % = [(MP − CP) / CP] × 100. It represents how much the price is raised above the cost price.
